English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
Guinean units of measurement
Wikipedia

Noun

[edit]

benda (plural bendas)

  1. An old Guinean unit of mass, equivalent to 0.0642 kilograms.

Bangi

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

benda

  1. to pull

Faroese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Norse benda, from Proto-Germanic *bandijaną, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ-.

Verb

[edit]

benda (third person singular past indicative bendi, third person plural past indicative bendu, supine bent)

  1. (grammar) to inflect

Conjugation

[edit]

supine bent

third singular bendir bendi

participle (a7)1 bendandi bendur
imperative
singular bend!
plural bendið!

1Only the past participle being declined.

Related terms

[edit]
  • benda á (to suggest; indicate)

Icelandic

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpɛnta/
  • Rhymes: -ɛnta

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Old Norse benda, from Proto-Germanic *bandijaną (“to bend”). Cognate with English bend.

Verb

[edit]

benda (weak verb, third-person singular past indicative benti, supine bent)

  1. (transitive) To bend.
  2. (transitive) To tie; join.
  3. (transitive) To strive; contest.
  4. (transitive, figurative) To give away.

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Old Norse benda, from Proto-Germanic *bandwijaną.

Verb

[edit]

benda (weak verb, third-person singular past indicative benti, supine bent)

  1. to point, to show
    Synonym: vísa

Derived terms
[edit]
  • ábending
  • benda á eitthvað, vísa á eitthvað (“to point at something”)
  • benda einhverju á eitthvað (“to point something out to someone”)

  • bendir

Indonesian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Malay benda (“a valuable thing”), from Sanskrit भाण्ड (bhāṇḍa, “good”). Doublet of banda. Cognate of Javanese ꦧꦤ꧀ꦝ (bandha).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /bənˈda/ [bənˈda]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -a
  • Syllabification: ben‧da

Noun

[edit]

bênda (plural benda-benda)

  1. object, good, etc
  2. thing
  3. valuable

Derived terms

[edit]
  • berbenda
  • kebendaan
  • membendakan
  • pembendaan
  • perbendaan
  • benda bergerak
  • benda cair
  • benda ekonomi
  • benda hidup
  • benda hitam
  • benda konsumsi
  • benda langit
  • benda mati
  • benda padat
  • benda tahan lama

Related terms

[edit]
  • banda
  • bangsal

Further reading

[edit]
  • “benda”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Proto-Zapotec *kw-ella, from Proto-Zapotecan *kw-ella.

Noun

[edit]

benda

  1. fish

Etymology 2

[edit]

From Proto-Zapotec *kw-ella.

Noun

[edit]

benda

  1. sister (of a female)

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbɛn.da/, /ˈben.da/[1]
  • Rhymes: -ɛnda, -enda
  • Hyphenation: bèn‧da, bén‧da

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Proto-Germanic *binda (“band, bind”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ-.[2]

Noun

[edit]

benda f (plural bende)

  1. bandage
  2. blindfold

benda

    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Malay

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • bende (pronunciation spelling)
  • bnde (text messaging)

Etymology

[edit]

From Sanskrit भाण्ड (bhāṇḍa, “good”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Baku) IPA(key): /bənˈda/ [bənˈda]
    • Rhymes: -ənda, -nda, -a
  • (schwa-variety) IPA(key): /bənˈdə/ [bənˈdə]
    • Rhymes: -əndə, -ndə, -ə
  • (Riau-Lingga) IPA(key): /ˈbən.da/
  • Hyphenation: ben‧da

Noun

[edit]

bĕnda (Jawi spelling بندا, plural benda-benda or benda2)

  1. object, good, etc.
  2. thing
  3. valuable

Derived terms

[edit]
  • berbenda
  • kebendaan
  • membendakan
  • pembendaan
  • perbendaan

Descendants

[edit]
  • > Indonesian: benda (inherited)
  • → Urak Lawoi': เบอนา (bena)
